title: US defaults on debt by 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the United States federal government fails to make a scheduled payment on any Treasury note, bond, or bill at any point between November 5, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, or Fitch publicly classify any U.S. sovereign debt as being in default during the qualifying period this will qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

The resolution source will be official information from the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, and Fitch.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders assign a 97.4% implied probability against a U.S. debt default by 2027 due to the long record of congressional debt-ceiling increases, most recently a $5 trillion hike in 2025 that set the current $41.1 trillion limit. Recent developments, including public debt crossing $40 trillion in August 2026 and Treasury buyback operations to stabilize yields, have not altered expectations that lawmakers will again resolve the mid-2027 borrowing constraint before extraordinary measures expire. Credit-rating agencies have affirmed or adjusted ratings while noting fiscal pressures from deficits and interest costs, yet historical precedent and the economic fallout of missed payments continue to anchor consensus. Scenarios that could still shift odds include an extended partisan standoff extending past the projected X-date or a sudden fiscal shock that exhausts cash buffers faster than anticipated.
